sources.entry: Home Assistant - Home automation platform. (Demo, Source Code) Apache-2.0 Python/Docker
Home Assistant | Open source home automation

summary.one_liner: Home Assistant Core is an open source home automation platform focused on local control and privacy, written to run on hardware like a Raspberry Pi or a local server.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Home Assistant as open source home automation that prioritizes local control and privacy. It is presented as suitable for running on a Raspberry Pi or a local server. The project uses a modular architecture so that support for new devices or actions can be added as components. The README links to external pages for a demo, installation instructions, tutorials, documentation, architecture notes, and guidance on creating custom components. It also points to a help section on the project website for troubleshooting. The README itself contains no installation commands, so details beyond these are not stated here.
use_cases: home automation on a Raspberry Pi
running a private home automation server
how_to_run: See the installation instructions on the project website (linked from the README; no commands are given in the README itself).
notable: Local control and privacy are the stated primary design goals
Modular component architecture for adding new devices and actions
Maintained by a worldwide community and part of the Open Home Foundation
Can run on a Raspberry Pi or a local server
caveats: The README does not give installation commands; setup is delegated to external documentation
Hardware and platform requirements are not detailed in the README
